sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 15.04.2015 passed by the Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.22/2013, on the grounds of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, negligence, and liability are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

3. As per the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Saraswati Bai in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.1,38,000/- along with interest in favour of claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4783 2 MA-1131-2015 4.

Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the learned Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased at a very low figure of Rs.2,000/- per month, ignoring the nature of work performed by the deceased and the prevailing economic conditions.

The deduction Shailendra Singh vs B.K. Jamhoriya on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188136643/
1 towards personal expenses has wrongly been made at 1/2 instead of 1/3 and the multiplier adopted is also on the lower side.
Further, the compensation awarded under the conventional heads as well as the rate of interest granted are inadequate.
As a result, the overall compensation awarded is unjust and deserves to be enhanced.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation based on the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves dismissal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
Upon consideration of the submissions and on perusal of the record, it is evident that the appellants failed to produce substantial documentary evidence regarding the income of the deceased.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down in Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi, (2008) 3 ACC 134 , where it is held that in absence of documentary proof, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the income of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4783 3 MA-1131-2015 deceased as that of an unskilled labourer.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the monthly income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.4,395/- per month as per the Minimum Wages Act.

8 . With regard to future prospects, in light of the judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled to future prospects at the rate of 10%.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as per Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. , (2009) 6 SCC 121, considering the age of the deceased, the appropriate multiplier of 9 has rightly been applied by Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. , (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Also, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131,
the claimants are entitled to get compensation towards loss of consortium and loss of estate.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.4395 x 12= Rs.52  After adding Future Prospects @10% Rs.58,014/-
 After deduction of Dependency 1/3 Rs.38,676/-
 Multiplier 9 Rs.3,48,084/-
 Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 2 = Rs.
Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total = Rs.4,58,084/-
10.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Shailendra Singh vs B.K. Jamhoriya on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188136643/
2 Rs.4,58,084/- as against the sum of Rs.1,38,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4783 4 MA-1131-2015 awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal. Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.3,20,084/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
11.
Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified, and the compensation is enhanced by Rs.3,20,084/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal and shall be paid within three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
All other conditions imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
13. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands modified and is partly allowed accordingly.
